question: What is the loop waiting on me for?
short: Go through the items the loop stopped on, one at a time: what each one is, where it stands, what the agent asks, and a recommendation you can accept with one choice.
lede: The loop stops where a person must decide. This skill puts each decision in front of you in plain words, records your answer on GitHub and hands the item back to the right agent, so the loop keeps moving without you reading every thread.
asks: Go through the needs-human items in uberblick-ai/uberblick-2.
What are the agents waiting on me for?
steps: Reads how the repository runs its loop: ub-agents.yaml, AGENTS.md and each agent's instructions, so labels, roles and merge policy come from your setup, not the defaults.
Lists stopped items with ub-agents status, highest priority and longest waiting first: items with a stop label such as needs-human, and blocked or failed runs.
Takes one item at a time and asks with an interactive prompt that stands on its own (see the example below).
Says exactly what it will change, then posts your answer and swaps the stop label for the label of the role that acts next. It can also merge a PR at the reviewed commit, approve, retry or close.

example.title: claude · uberblick-2
example.caption: A run in uberblick-ai/uberblick-2, trimmed to the first item.

turns.say: Four issues wait on a decision (#1887, #1871, #1847, #1850). Four more are blocked and need nothing from you. Starting with #1887, the highest priority.
The agent asks whether to leave the hub-to-local case out of #1887. I agree: it is rare and would bloat a focused security fix. It can be filed separately.

turns.ask: https://github.com/uberblick-ai/uberblick-2/issues/1887 stops a repo's .uberblick.json from silently syncing your replica with a different hub. When the record says hub but the binding says local, how should the refusal handle it?
options: Leave hub-to-local out. The refusal points back to the recorded selection.
Add a hub-to-local command to #1887. Makes the issue bigger.

turns.say: Commented 1A on #1887, removed needs-human and added needs-preparation. The issue preparer picks it up next. On to #1871.

facts: the issue or PR as a clickable GitHub URL
one plain sentence on what the item changes for users
what is done, what is blocking it and what the decision unblocks, without file names or check output
what the stopped agent asked, for reference
the skill's own pick from the item and your repository's guidance, marked first, and why it differs from the agent's when it does
up to four, or your own answer in your words
needs: an authenticated gh acting as a maintainer.
ub-agents in the repository's checkout, to list blocked and failed runs too.
only what you choose: a comment, labels, a milestone, a merge or a close.
